```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(knitr.graphics.rel_path = FALSE)
analysis_root <- normalizePath(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
  mustWork = TRUE
)
results_dir <- file.path(analysis_root, "results")
plots_dir <- file.path(analysis_root, "plots")
read_result <- function(name) {
  data.table::fread(file.path(results_dir, name), data.table = FALSE)
}
show_table <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  knitr::kable(x, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)
}
candidate <- read_result("candidate_evidence.csv")
flow <- read_result("sample_flow.csv")
covariates <- read_result("covariate_eligibility.csv")
de_summary <- read_result("de_contrast_summary.csv")
mapping <- read_result("mapping_audit.csv")
enrichment_metadata <- read_result("enrichment_run_metadata.csv")
depmap_metadata <- read_result("depmap_run_metadata.csv")
warnings <- data.table::fread(
  file.path(analysis_root, "provenance", "warnings.csv"),
  data.table = FALSE
)
```

# Scope and interpretation

This corrected workflow uses the frozen local TCGA-BRCA STAR-count, clinical,
and DepMap snapshots to nominate TNBC targets. It separates expression,
sensitivity-analysis, dependency, selectivity, common-essential, and
tractability evidence. The output is a prioritization resource, not evidence of
causality, clinical efficacy, or safety.

# Frozen inputs and provenance

All expression counts were read offline from 1,224 checksum-recorded local
files. A single metadata-only GDC query was frozen to map file UUIDs to samples;
normal reruns require that local response and do not query GDC. Enrichment used
only locally installed annotation collections.

```{r enrichment-sources}
show_table(enrichment_metadata)
```

# Cohort construction

Primary tumors were called TNBC only when ER, PR, and HER2 were all recorded as
negative. Normals were assigned from GDC sample type independently of receptor
fields. One sample per patient and analysis group was selected by a deterministic
barcode rule. The primary comparison is all eligible TNBC tumors versus all
eligible solid-tissue normals; the paired comparison is a sensitivity analysis.

```{r cohort-flow}
show_table(flow)
```

```{r pca, fig.cap="PCA of the primary TNBC and normal cohort; the embedded plot caption reports the transformation and group sizes."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "pca_primary.png"))
```

# Differential-expression models

The numerator is TNBC in every contrast. Genes were filtered within each
contrast, modeled with DESeq2, and effect sizes were shrunk with apeglm. Candidate
expression evidence requires primary FDR below 0.05 and shrunken log2 fold change
above 1. Age was scaled before modeling when eligible.

```{r de-summary}
show_table(de_summary)
```

## Covariate decisions

Covariates were included only when sufficiently complete and not group-confounded.
Patient identity was used as a block in the paired model.

```{r covariates}
show_table(covariates)
```

```{r volcano, fig.cap="Primary TNBC-minus-normal differential expression; thresholds and sample sizes are stated in the plot caption."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "volcano_primary.png"))
```

## Sensitivity analyses

Positive paired and specificity effects are recorded as directional concordance,
not as replacement primary tests. Missing estimates remain explicitly unavailable.

```{r paired, fig.cap="Paired-versus-primary effect concordance."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "concordance_paired_primary.png"))
```

```{r specificity, fig.cap="Specificity-versus-primary effect concordance."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "concordance_specificity_primary.png"))
```

# Enrichment and mapping losses

ORA used direction-specific primary genes and the tested, mapped background for
each collection. Ranked enrichment used the full finite primary statistic. The
mapping audit below bounds interpretation of both analyses.

```{r mapping-audit}
show_table(mapping)
```

```{r enrichment-go-up, fig.cap="GO biological-process ORA for primary upregulated genes; the plot caption states the contrast, samples, thresholds, and universe."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "enrichment_go_up.png"))
```

```{r enrichment-go-down, fig.cap="GO biological-process ORA for primary downregulated genes; the plot caption states the contrast, samples, thresholds, and universe."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "enrichment_go_down.png"))
```

```{r enrichment-kegg-up, fig.cap="KEGG-legacy ORA for primary upregulated genes; the plot caption states the contrast, samples, thresholds, and universe."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "enrichment_kegg_up.png"))
```

```{r enrichment-kegg-down, fig.cap="KEGG-legacy ORA for primary downregulated genes; the plot caption states the contrast, samples, thresholds, and universe."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "enrichment_kegg_down.png"))
```

# DepMap dependency evidence

Model inclusion used literal local subtype labels: TNBC models versus explicitly
ER-positive or HER2-positive breast comparators. The exact DepMap release could
not be recovered from local source files and is therefore unresolved. Gene-effect
summaries are model-level; no probability table was substituted.

```{r depmap-metadata}
show_table(depmap_metadata)
```

```{r depmap-plot, fig.cap="TNBC-versus-comparator median DepMap gene effects; panel sizes and thresholds appear in the plot caption."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plots_dir, "depmap_tnbc_vs_non_tnbc.png"))
```

# Candidate evidence classes

No arithmetic score is used. Class A requires primary upregulation, both
sensitivity directions, TNBC dependency, TNBC-selective dependency, and absence
from the frozen common-essential list. Class B requires primary upregulation,
TNBC dependency, and at least one sensitivity direction. Remaining primary hits
are Class C. Tractability is **not assessed** because the configured evidence
table is intentionally empty; this must not be interpreted as “not druggable.”

```{r class-counts}
class_counts <- as.data.frame(table(candidate$evidence_class), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(class_counts) <- c("evidence_class", "genes")
show_table(class_counts)
```

```{r top-candidates}
top_candidates <- candidate[
  candidate$evidence_class %in% c("A_multistream", "B_expression_dependency"),
  c(
    "ensembl_id", "gene_symbol", "evidence_class", "primary_padj",
    "primary_log2fc_shrunk", "paired_log2fc_shrunk",
    "specificity_log2fc_shrunk", "tnbc_median_effect",
    "tnbc_fraction_below_threshold", "tnbc_minus_non_tnbc",
    "common_essential", "tractability_assessment"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]
show_table(utils::head(top_candidates, 30))
```

# Warnings and limitations

```{r warnings}
show_table(warnings)
```

Additional limitations include cross-sectional bulk-tissue composition,
clinical-annotation error, residual technical or site effects, gene-symbol-based
joining to DepMap, and the lack of experimental validation. Candidate classes
are transparent evidence summaries for follow-up, not claims of therapeutic
actionability.

# Reproduction

Run `Rscript analysis_v2/run_all.R` after loading R 4.4.2. Input, source, output,
package, session, warning, and per-stage provenance records are stored under
`analysis_v2/provenance/`.
